acceptance.criterion_verbatim: THE REFUSE BRANCH: when a file's suffix is in the gate's DECLARED read set (.py / .sh / .tf / org/projects/*.json) and the file received ZERO checks, the gate exits a DISTINCT non-zero rc (rc=2, named in the header) with the same "NOTHING WAS CHECKED" text -- never rc=0. The operator then names the instrument actually used or widens the scope deliberately.
acceptance.invocation: In .tools/commit_gate_runner.py: a `declared` counter incremented INSIDE each of the four declared dispatch branches; at the tail, `if checked == 0:` prints the unchanged NOTHING WAS CHECKED block and then, `if declared:`, a REFUSED line and `return 2`. Exercised by a mutant of .tools/commit_gate_runner.py carrying ONLY the removal of the .sh branch's `checked += 1`, run against data/.zerocheck_scratch/clean.sh, with the shipped runner on the same file as the control.
acceptance.output_evidence: MUTANT: 'OK: bash -n syntax-checked ...' then 'WARN: commit-gate checked 0 of 1 file(s) -- NOTHING WAS CHECKED.' (same text, unchanged) then 'REFUSED (rc=2): 1 of 1 file(s) carry a suffix this gate DECLARES it reads (.py / .sh / .tf / org/projects/*.json), and NOTHING was checked on any of them. A declared subject reaching zero checks is a GATE DEFECT, not a clean commit -- rc=2 exists so it can never be read as a pass.' rc=2. CONTROL, shipped runner, same file: 'OK: pre-commit gate clean for 1 of 1 file(s)', rc=0 -- so the rc=2 is caused by the removed counter, not by the subject. THE COUNTER IS COUNTED IN THE DISPATCH, NOT RE-DERIVED AT THE TAIL: a second predicate describing the same set would fail OPEN, which is this bug's own shape.
acceptance.denominator: 4 of 4 declared dispatch branches carry `declared += 1` (verified by parsing the file and listing the increment line of each branch); 1 mutant + 1 control.
acceptance.status_reason: PASS on the branch's behaviour, with a disclosure the grader should have: the branch is UNREACHABLE through today's dispatch, because all four declared branches also increment `checked` (verified, same parse). It is a REGRESSION GUARD whose value is prospective -- it catches the next branch that forgets to count, which is exactly how this defect was born -- and I exercised it with the mutant rather than shipping an unfired branch and calling it a control.

acceptance.status_reason: One instrument failure of MINE inside this criterion, recorded because it nearly became evidence: my first REPRODUCTION of the (iii) baseline ran the saved pre-fix runner from the scratchpad, where its sibling imports do not resolve. The difference is attributable to the removed counter and nothing else, because the subject, the runner and the invocation are otherwise identical. SECOND, INDEPENDENT MUTANT-SHAPED ARM: the pre-fix runner itself is a natural mutant of the fix, and on the twin subjects it produced byte-identical rc=0 output for a broken and a clean file -- the defect demonstrated on the real artifact rather than a synthetic one.

surprises: BLOCKING / SHAPE QUESTION TO 1.0.0_SA_CTO (owner of the ruling), ARMED: THIS INSTANCE CANNOT BE MADE VALID WITHOUT FABRICATING DATA, AND I HAVE NOT FABRICATED IT. proof-of-spec-check decides alignment enforcement on the mere PRESENCE of a <decomp_ref> TAG in the governing TO -- has_decomp_ref = (blob is not None) at :473, harvested by the regex at :428; :623 takes the ANNOUNCE branch (decomp_ref NOT required) only when the TO carries NO tag, otherwise :640 ENFORCEs and :663 requires every criterion to carry cell_refs. THIS TO CARRIES THE TAG AND ITS TEXT IS 'NONE -- a one-branch remediation of an existing tool under its own charter', and its five criteria are written <criterion id="ZC-n"/> with no cell_refs, because there is no decomposition to reference. So the checker demands cell_refs that do not exist, while itself refusing them: ':663 -- REFUSED, never retrofitted: a derived cell_ref makes alignment LOOK satisfied while being FALSE'. Verdict on this instance: INVALID, rc=1 (UNPIPED), checker @3948c766a7, violations = the five cell_ref rows and nothing else -- every structural, artifact-coverage, artifact-resolution and vintage check passes. I am delivering it in that state deliberately. The remedy is a SHAPE call and belongs to the gate, not to this seat: either the TO omits the <decomp_ref> element (taking the ANNOUNCE branch it was written for) or the checker distinguishes a tag whose body DECLARES no decomposition from one that names cells. This is precisely the pattern 1.0.0_SA_CTO ruled at 87632 for the absent register row -- if the tooling cannot roll the face up, print it as a finding against the tooling, do not mint a member no directive named. A fabricated cell_ref would be that mint, one layer down.
